llm.summary: This skill is a local travel safety lookup tool with no data collection or system-changing behavior, though users should verify travel risks with current official advisories.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to check, rank, and compare destination safety ratings, and the artifact implements exactly those functions using an embedded destination database.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime inputs are narrowly scoped to destination names, regions, or comma-separated comparisons; the main caveat is that travel safety information is static and may become outdated.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains a SKILL.md, VERSION file, and a Python helper script; no install hooks, dependency installation, startup behavior, or automatic execution were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The script imports only json and sys, reads command-line arguments, and prints results from local data; it does not use network access, credentials, local files, or user data stores.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No persistence, background workers, privilege escalation, file writes, deletion, or mutation authority were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a static, built-in reference for destination safety comparisons. Treat the ratings as general guidance, not real-time safety advice, and check current government or embassy travel advisories before making travel decisions.
llm.findings:
[SkillSpector clean report] expected: SkillSpector reported no issues, which matches the artifact evidence of a small local lookup script.
[Static scan clean report] expected: Static scan reported no suspicious findings; manual inspection found no network calls, credential handling, persistence, or unsafe command execution.
